llm.reply:
KRAS encodes a small GTPase that functions as a molecular switch in signal transduction, and its oncogenic mutations drive constitutive pathway activation across multiple cancer types [11].

## GTPase Molecular Function

The KRAS gene product belongs to the small GTPase superfamily, acting as a molecular switch that regulates downstream signaling pathways controlling cell proliferation and survival [11][26]. A single amino acid substitution can produce an activating mutation, resulting in a transforming protein implicated in lung adenocarcinoma, pancreatic ductal carcinoma, and colorectal carcinoma [11]. In colorectal cancer, KRAS mutations occur in approximately 40% of cases and cause constitutive activation of the KRAS protein, persistently stimulating proliferation and survival signaling [26].

## Oncogenic Signaling in Cancer

Oncogenic KRAS contributes to multiple cancer hallmarks, including suppression of antitumor immunity and promotion of tumor invasion and metastasis in colorectal cancer [28]. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, KRAS is mutated in up to 90% of cases, with the G12D, G12V, and G12R variants predominating [29]. The protein's GTPase activity is central to its oncogenic mechanism, as mutant KRAS remains in an active GTP-bound state, driving tumorigenesis through sustained pathway activation [26][27].

## Therapeutic Targeting of KRAS GTPase

KRAS was historically considered undruggable, but allele-specific inhibitors targeting the G12C mutation, including sotorasib and adagrasib, have achieved clinical efficacy [27][29]. Small-molecule degraders designed to eliminate oncogenic KRAS protein have demonstrated tumor regression in vivo, offering a complementary strategy beyond direct enzymatic inhibition [30].

The KRAS gene product functions as a small GTPase, a member of the small GTPase superfamily, acting as a molecular switch that stimulates downstream signaling pathways including cell proliferation and survival [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"][26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. The OMIM record titles the gene KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. Activating mutations produce a transforming protein implicated in lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas, and colorectal carcinoma [11: "The transforming protein that results is implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"].

## Gene Identity and Nomenclature

The gene symbol is KRAS [1], the gene name is KRAS [5], and the literature entity name is Kras [6]. Alternative splicing produces two isoforms differing in the C-terminal region [11: "Alternative splicing leads to variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].
